title: 3-D Plot
description: Answer a few questions and watch the TRS-80 draw a funnel-shaped 3-D surface as a wire grid, one dot at a time.
versionOrder: Inferred development sequence, not established dates. v01 and v02 are tape19b saves 2 and 10, in that save order. v02 replaces v01's LINE statement (not in Level II BASIC; most likely from Microsoft's cassette Level III BASIC) with a line-drawing subroutine that v03 keeps verbatim at lines 360-420. My recollection (2026-10-31, tentative): I probably dropped LINE so that more people, most of whom had only Level II, could run the program and see the picture; v03 restores v01's surface and adds the prompts and the 1979 credit. Tape numbers alone do not establish chronology.

versions.label: Draft · Surface with LINE
versions.note: A funnel-shaped surface drawn as a 7 × 7 wire grid with the LINE statement. No prompts or title.
versions.unavailableReason: Source only. LINE is not a Level II BASIC statement: on the site's Model III Level II BASIC this version stops with ?L3 Error in 150. Its payload was saved with a higher program start (pointer base 22204, not Level II's 17125), so it was probably written under a BASIC extension loaded into memory below the program. The most likely is Microsoft's Level III BASIC, a cassette add-on to Level II whose additions included LINE for drawing lines and boxes (TRSDOS Disk BASIC had no graphics LINE). That environment was not recovered.

versions.label: Draft · Own line drawing, flat test grid
versions.note: Replaces LINE with a line-drawing subroutine of SET calls, so it runs in Level II BASIC. The surface is set to Y=0, so it draws a flat tilted grid, apparently to test the new routine.
versions.unavailableReason: Source only. On this site the Level II BASIC player runs v03, the finished version; this listing and payload remain downloadable.

versions.label: 3-D PLOT (C) 1979 · Prompts
versions.note: Adds the title and credit, prompts for tilt, X and Y scale, a SWITCH option and the number of grid lines (ENTER keeps each default), and restores the funnel surface.
